newsitem.title: USA: Dakota track plan seen as challenge to rail rivals.
newsitem.headline: Dakota track plan seen as challenge to rail rivals.

text.p: Dakota, Minnesota & Eastern Railroad Corp's (DM&E) planned $1.2 billion expansion could pose a threat to Burlington Northern Santa Fe Corp and Union Pacific Corp, though it remains to be seen if DM&E will secure the necessary financing, analysts said on Monday.

Earlier, DM&E said it planned to build about 250 miles of railroad track to extend its service into the Powder River Basin in Wyoming, a major coal-producing area. It also plans to rebuild about 650 miles of track.
"It's a thorn in the side of both Western coal carriers," Natwest Markets analyst Anthony Hatch said of DM&E's project.
But he added that, since it is a long-term project, the expansion plan does not pose an immediate threat.
Hatch said financing also poses a major obstacle for the $1.2 billion project. "Financing is the primary concern," Hatch said.
DM&E said it expected the project to be completed within five years.
"It's a long-term project," PNC Asset Management Group analyst Charles Vincent said. "The big railroads will have an opportunity to prepare for what will probably be an assault to their business."

DM&E said it retained Morgan Stanley & Co to assist in identifying strategic partners in the expansion project. Analysts said potential partners could come from outside the rail industry, possibly even utilities that use the low-sulfur coal mined in the Powder River Basin.

Even before the project is built, DM&E's proposed service could work in favor of existing rail line customers, analysts said. To prepare for the potential competition, Burlington Northern and Union Pacific could offer further incentives to customers.
"This works for customers at this point even before (DM&E's expansion) gets built," Hatch said.
